newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Zaire's Mobutu expected in Morocco soon - diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu expected in Morocco soon - diplomat.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko is expected in Morocco in the next 48 hours and appears to have chosen the North African country as his place of exile, a Western diplomat said on Friday.

"According to the latest information we have, Mobutu will visit Morocco in the coming 48 hours...It seems that he has chosen Morocco as a place for exile," the diplomat, who declined to be named, told Reuters. He gave no further details and there was no official confirmation.
A foreign ministry official would neither confirm nor deny that Mobutu was heading for exile in Morocco.
Morocco's King Hassan met Mobutu in Rabat last February.
At that time, Mobutu said he had not come to Morocco to seek military aid in his battle against rebels, as was reported by the local press.

A staunch ally of Mobutu, Morocco sent troops to Zaire to put down a 1977 secessionist uprising in Shaba after Zairean forces were overwhelmed. They also relieved French and Belgian paratroops backing Zairean authorities in the mining town of Kolwezi the following year.
